correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the weak-contraction expansion. Along a two-sided Poisson process the stationary age and earlier gaps are iid Exp(1); the stable increments across those intervals have characteristic exponents weighted by c^(jα). The sum of conditional stable scale times is almost surely finite, yielding the stationary scale mixture with normalized time V=δ Σ_j (1−δ)^j E_j. Coupling two initial states with the same resets and noise multiplies their difference by c to the number of resets, which tends to zero, proving uniqueness. The weights sum to one; sums of their rth powers times (r−1)! give the cumulants, so Var(V)=δ/(2−δ) and E(V−1)^4=3 Var(V)^2+6δ^4/(1−(1−δ)^4)=O(δ²). Hence E|V−1|³=O(δ^(3/2)). The needed three L1 derivatives in v can also be justified without the cited stable tail estimate: subordinate the Gaussian p_(2,s) with s=v^(2/α)T where T has Laplace transform exp(−u^(α/2)) (T=1 for α=2). Gaussian scaling gives ||∂_s^j p_(2,s)||_1=const_j s^(−j); after the chain rule the factors T^j cancel these negative powers of T, providing uniform L1 domination on [1/2,3/2]. The first Taylor term averages to zero and the quadratic term has exact coefficient Var(V)/2. Outside the interval, 2 bounds the density difference in L1 and the constant, linear and quadratic tail contributions are all O(δ²) by the fourth moment and |V−1|>1/2. Fourier differentiation gives the stated K_α, nonzero but integral zero, hence sign-changing. For Cauchy, a primitive of K_1 is 2x/[π(1+x²)²] and the sign boundary is 1/√3. For Gaussian, K_2=p_2 H_4(x/√2)/4 and the boundary contributions from −H_3 φ at a and b give ||K_2||_1=√6[aφ(a)+bφ(b)]. Halving the density error yields ||K_α||_1 ε_c/4 plus the stated remainder. The index is fixed; no uniformity or finite state variance for α<2 is needed. Inspected the frozen verification/check.py and its 171-assertion saved output without executing the upload; finite Fourier checks do not certify the L1 remainder.

value.rationale: Weak resetting is a natural singular limit of the stationary family. The signed L1 correction gives the first measurable error in replacing a random operational time by its mean, valid even when the stable state lacks a variance. Strict positivity of the TV coefficient makes the order sharp, and the two tractable endpoints supply exact benchmarks not available from characteristic-function convergence alone.
